first_impression.reaction: Our daughter sent this, and I'll be honest, Brazil worries me before I start. The first paragraph answers the important bit: yes, it's legal for them. I read it top to bottom on the iPad. It's careful and it quotes the government, which I like, but it's heavy going. There are a lot of Portuguese words to keep straight, and the legal part keeps telling the children to ask the cartório themselves. Then the safety section frightened me: violent crime, muggings, drink spiking, Copacabana named as a hotspot. The insurance, deposits and step-free questions are exactly right. What it never tells me is who looks after the family when we land, or who I ring if something goes wrong.

journey.quote: Yes, getting married in Brazil is open to foreign couples, and the legal part happens through a civil process at a Cartório de Registro Civil, the civil registry office.
journey.reaction: Good, a straight answer at the top. Geoff's first question will be whether it's legal, and that's answered.

journey.quote: What follows is the order to work in: documents first, then the cartório, then the certificate you bring home.
journey.reaction: Three steps in order. I can follow that and explain it to Geoff.

journey.section: Can foreigners legally marry in Brazil?
journey.quote: If neither of you lives in Brazil, ask the registry office directly how it applies the district rule to couples who live abroad, and which office should take your application.
journey.reaction: So it isn't settled? If the rule is that one of them has to live there, I'd want someone who knows the answer, not the children ringing a Brazilian office in Portuguese.

journey.section: Public notice and how long approval lasts
journey.quote: The public notice of your intention to marry is called the proclamas, the banns.
journey.reaction: Habilitação, cartório, proclamas, tradutor juramentado. I've had to go back twice to remember which is which. I'm getting a bit lost.

journey.quote: In Brazil, foreign documents, even when apostilled, must be translated by a tradutor juramentado, a sworn public translator, to be valid, and that translation can only be done in Brazil.
journey.reaction: Useful to know, but it's exactly what I fear: papers in another language, done over there. Who finds the translator, and how do we know they're proper?

journey.section: Civil ceremony, religious ceremony or both?
journey.quote: Ask the cartório to explain the property regime options before the day, so you choose rather than default.
journey.reaction: Now that's something I'd never have known. A property regime decided at the ceremony matters when we're putting money in. I'll make sure Geoff reads that line.

journey.section: Will a Brazilian marriage be recognised in Australia?
journey.quote: For Australians: you cannot register an overseas marriage in Australia, but in most cases it is legally recognised if it was valid under the law of the country where it took place and would have been valid under Australian law had it happened here.
journey.reaction: Clear, and it points to Smartraveller. That's what I need to forward.

journey.quote: You may need a valid yellow fever vaccination certificate to enter Brazil, and some airlines may ask for a copy when you depart.
journey.reaction: Mum would need to see her doctor about that well ahead. Good that it's said, but it's one more hurdle for the older ones.

journey.quote: It says violent crime including mugging, armed robbery and carjacking is common, more often in large cities and during festivals such as Carnival, and advises against going out alone at night and against isolated areas, including beaches.
journey.reaction: This is the paragraph that would stop me. I'm glad it's honest, but against beaches? Then why is the page full of beach ceremonies? Nothing after it says who keeps our family safe.

journey.quote: **Deposits:** whose name is on the contract, and when do deposits become non-refundable?
journey.reaction: There it is. Whose name, and when the money is gone. That's my question.

journey.quote: **Access:** which ceremony, dining and guest spaces have step-free access?
journey.reaction: Mum and her walking frame. Someone thought about us.

journey.quote: **Security:** how does your security work for any couple marrying here, and how would it work alongside security we bring?
journey.reaction: Security we bring? We're not bringing bodyguards. After the crime paragraph this makes me more nervous, not less.

journey.section: How much does it cost to get married in Brazil?
journey.quote: Your guests will need travel insurance, because Smartraveller says private health care in larger cities is very expensive and that cover must include all medical costs, including evacuation.
journey.reaction: Sensible and specific. Evacuation cover for the older ones, noted.

journey.section: How much does it cost to get married in Brazil?
journey.quote: On the paperwork side, a fee applies for an Australian CNI and for the Embassy's notarial services.
journey.reaction: A fee applies, but how much? There isn't a single dollar figure in the cost section. I'd like a rough idea before I agree to anything.

journey.quote: Smartraveller names Copacabana Beach, Ipanema Beach, the Pedra do Sal area, Santa Teresa, Lapa, the Christ the Redeemer statue and the Corcovado Trail as crime hotspots.
journey.reaction: Those are the places anyone would want photos. Honest, but I'm now picturing the bridal party being robbed at Christ the Redeemer.

journey.quote: A Wedded Advisor plans the venue, travel, vendors and payments with you as one point of contact from start to finish, working in your time zone and quoting in AUD, with the fee agreed in writing before any work begins.
journey.reaction: One person, AUD, fee in writing first. That's what I want with our money, especially somewhere like this. I'd still want a name and a phone call.

unanswered_questions: Who do we ring if something goes wrong in Brazil, after hours? Is anyone from Wedded Wonderland there on the day? (deferred business detail)
Do you arrange safe airport transfers for guests, including an elderly guest with a walking frame? (deferred business detail)
Does Wedded Wonderland deal with the cartório, translator and paperwork, or is that all on the couple?
Are our deposits protected if a Brazilian venue or supplier, or Wedded Wonderland itself, fails?
Roughly what do the CNI, notarial fees, translations and cartório cost, in AUD? (fee amounts deferred)
Can couples who don't live in Brazil actually apply, given the residence wording?
How is your fee charged, and do you take commissions from venues? (deferred business detail)
Is the first conversation a phone call with a real person, and can I join it as a parent paying part?
Have you planned real weddings in Brazil I could look at? (deferred business detail)

turn_offs_found.quote: It says violent crime including mugging, armed robbery and carjacking is common, more often in large cities and during festivals such as Carnival, and advises against going out alone at night and against isolated areas, including beaches.
turn_offs_found.why: Not a tone problem; it's calm and quotes the government. But the crime, drink spiking and hotspots run on with nothing after them about who looks after the family. My biggest fear is raised and left hanging.

turn_offs_found.quote: So a ceremony on sand, a clifftop lawn or a fazenda veranda starts as a conversation with the cartório.
turn_offs_found.why: Most of the legal sections end by handing the children another question to ask an office in Portuguese. It reads like a to-do list for them rather than help, and that's the contract-in-another-language worry I have.

turn_offs_found.quote: **Security:** how does your security work for any couple marrying here, and how would it work alongside security we bring?
turn_offs_found.why: It assumes we bring our own security. That makes me feel the page is written for someone far richer than us, and after the crime paragraph it adds worry.

would_share_with: My husband, the intro, the recognition section and the property regime line, plus the deposits question
My mother, the yellow fever and travel insurance lines, so she sees her doctor early and gets proper cover
My daughter, the step-free access question and the Smartraveller safety advice, so she picks somewhere safe for Nana

cta_reaction.quote: Your Wedded Advisor stays with you from start to finish, works in your time zone, quotes in AUD, and confirms inclusions in writing before you commit.
cta_reaction.why: The right words: AUD, in writing, start to finish. Brazil feels harder and riskier after this than before, so I'd only go further with someone in charge. I'd talk to Geoff first, and I'd want a phone call with a real person who can tell me who meets the family, who deals with the Portuguese paperwork, and how our deposits are protected.

top_3_changes: After the safety section, add one calm line on what Wedded Concierge does to keep guests safe on the ground (transfers, on-the-day contact), but only if the business confirms it; otherwise flag it. The crime advice currently ends with no reassurance.
Say plainly whether a Wedded Advisor helps with the cartório, sworn translator and Portuguese paperwork, if confirmed. The legal sections keep handing the couple questions to ask in another language.
Reword the security item so it doesn't assume a private team, move it below deposits and access, and add a short glossary or recap line for habilitação, cartório and proclamas.

checks.check: Every journey point and turn-off has an exact quote from the draft
Journey types limited to gained_trust, lost_trust, confused, bored, excited, objection
Stayed in character as Margaret (funding parent): read top to bottom on iPad, focused on deposits, who is responsible, elderly guests, safety, insurance and a phone call
No invented brand facts; on-the-day support, transfers, paperwork help, deposit protection, fees and real weddings placed in unanswered_questions
VERIFY markers and HTML comments (fact tags, image slots) ignored

open_questions.question: Can the business confirm on-the-day support, guest transfers and help with cartório paperwork so one reassuring line can follow the safety section? If not, flag rather than fill.

assumptions: Margaret arrived via a link from her daughter, reading on an iPad, as a parent contributing about half. Relevance is 3 because the page is a legal how-to written to the couple, though it covers insurance, step-free access and deposits.
Clarity is 3: the order is clear, but the run of Portuguese terms and repeated 'ask the cartório' makes it hard going for her.
Likelihood to enquire is 3: AUD and fee-in-writing earn trust, but the safety section raises fears nothing answers. Missing on-the-day help is a deferred business detail, not penalised as must-fix.
Her mother's walking frame comes from the persona card; husband's name (Geoff) is character colour consistent with earlier panels, not a page fact.
Fast mode: full article read top to bottom, FAQ skimmed as it repeats the body.
